igcse-0580-powers-squares.description: Use square facts and read exactly what the square-root sign and brackets mean.

sections.title: How do square areas help?
sections.label: Build it
sections.intro: Arrange unit squares in equal rows and columns. A square with side 7 has seven rows of seven tiles.

blocks.html: Find the two equal sides and multiply them. Area is measured in square units.

figure.alt: A three-by-three array beside a five-by-five array
figure.caption: Count rows and columns separately, then multiply.

blocks.prompt: A square banner is 12 cm wide. Work out its area in square centimetres.
blocks.hint: A square has equal sides. Multiply the side length by itself.
blocks.solution:
The height and width both equal 12 cm.

\(12^2=12\times12=144\).

The completed square covers 144 square centimetres.

retry.feedback: That doubles the side length. The area uses two factors of the side length.

blocks.html: Doubling the side only finds two side lengths.

blocks.prompt: A square banner is 15 cm wide. Work out its area in square centimetres.
blocks.hint: A square has equal sides. Multiply the side length by itself.
blocks.solution:
The height and width both equal 15 cm.

\(15^2=15\times15=225\).

The completed square covers 225 square centimetres.

retry.feedback: That doubles the side length. The area uses two factors of the side length.

sections.title: How do I reverse a square?
sections.label: Undo it
sections.intro: Read the root sign as a request for the non-negative side length. Link it to a square fact you know.

blocks.html: Know the squares from 1 through 15 and recognise the same facts in reverse.

blocks.hint: Find the matching square fact.
blocks.solution:
Find the non-negative number whose square is 121.

\(11\times11=121\) shows that 11 works.

Write 11. The square-root sign names the non-negative value.

retry.feedback: The negative value also squares to the number. The root sign asks for the non-negative one.

blocks.html: The standalone square-root sign does not ask for both signs.

blocks.hint: Find the matching square fact.
blocks.solution:
Find the non-negative number whose square is 196.

\(14\times14=196\) shows that 14 works.

Write 14. The square-root sign names the non-negative value.

retry.feedback: The negative value also squares to the number. The root sign asks for the non-negative one.

sections.title: What happens to a minus sign?
sections.label: Brackets
sections.intro: Put a finger under the base. A bracketed negative base is repeatedly multiplied with its sign. A minus outside the power is applied after the power.

blocks.html: Read the grouping before you calculate.

blocks.hint: Check whether the minus sign is inside or outside brackets.
blocks.solution:
The exponent belongs to the positive number. Apply the minus sign after squaring.

\(-(11\times 11)=-121\).

The signed value is \(-121\).

retry.feedback: Include the minus sign in the base only if it is grouped in brackets.

blocks.html: A calculator must be told which terms the brackets contain.

blocks.hint: Check whether the minus sign is inside or outside brackets.
blocks.solution:
The brackets make the negative number the base. Both factors are negative.

\((-14)\times(-14)=196\).

The signed value is \(196\).

retry.feedback: Include the minus sign in the base only if it is grouped in brackets.

igcse-0580-powers-cubes.description: Build a cube in layers and reverse its volume calculation.

sections.title: Why multiply three times?
sections.label: Layers
sections.intro: Choose an edge length. Each flat square layer has that many rows and columns. Stack the same number of layers.

blocks.html: The volume in cubic units is the edge length cubed.

figure.alt: Four separate layers, each containing four rows of four tiles
figure.caption: Stacking the four square layers builds a cube.

blocks.prompt: A cube has edge length 6 cm. Find its volume in cubic centimetres.
blocks.hint: Multiply three copies of the edge length.
blocks.solution:
One layer has \(6\times6=36\) unit cubes.

There are 6 layers. Multiply by 6 again.

The volume is \(6^3=216\) cubic centimetres.

retry.feedback: This is one layer. Multiply by the number of layers.

blocks.html: The square of the edge only counts one layer.

blocks.prompt: A cube has edge length 9 cm. Find its volume in cubic centimetres.
blocks.hint: Multiply three copies of the edge length.
blocks.solution:
One layer has \(9\times9=81\) unit cubes.

There are 9 layers. Multiply by 9 again.

The volume is \(9^3=729\) cubic centimetres.

retry.feedback: This is one layer. Multiply by the number of layers.

sections.title: How do I recover an edge?
sections.label: Edges
sections.intro: Look for the number that multiplies by itself twice to give a cube volume. The small 3 at the root sign means cube root.

blocks.html: Remember the cubes of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 alongside their roots.

BaseCube
11

blocks.prompt: A model cube has volume 1000 cubic centimetres. Find its edge length in centimetres.
blocks.hint: Use a cube root because you are reversing three equal factors.
blocks.solution:
The edge appears three times in the volume calculation.

\(10\times10\times10=1000\) proves that 10 works.

The cube root is \(\sqrt[3]{1000}=10\). The edge is 10 cm.

blocks.html: A square root would reverse two factors. Here there are three.

blocks.prompt: A model cube has volume 27 cubic centimetres. Find its edge length in centimetres.
blocks.hint: Use a cube root because you are reversing three equal factors.
blocks.solution:
The edge appears three times in the volume calculation.

\(3\times3\times3=27\) proves that 3 works.

The cube root is \(\sqrt[3]{27}=3\). The edge is 3 cm.

sections.title: Can a cube root be negative?
sections.label: Negative
sections.intro: Two negative factors give a positive product. The third negative factor makes the product negative again.

blocks.html: A negative number has exactly one real cube root.

blocks.hint: Choose the sign first. Then match the size using a cube fact.
blocks.solution:
A positive base cubed is positive. A negative base cubed is negative.

\((-10)\times(-10)\times(-10)=-1000\) .

The only real cube root is \(-10\).

retry.feedback: The positive base produces a positive cube. Keep the negative sign.

blocks.html: The small 3 belongs to the root sign. It does not multiply the root.

blocks.hint: Choose the sign first. Then match the size using a cube fact.
blocks.solution:
A positive base cubed is positive. A negative base cubed is negative.

\((-3)\times(-3)\times(-3)=-27\) .

The only real cube root is \(-3\).

retry.feedback: The positive base produces a positive cube. Keep the negative sign.

igcse-0580-powers-higher.description: Count copies of a base, then undo a fourth, fifth or sixth power.

sections.title: What do the small and large numbers mean?
sections.label: Copies
sections.intro: The large number is the base. The small exponent tells you how many copies of the base to multiply.

blocks.html: Say the repeated multiplication before using a calculator key.

figure.alt: Two passes through a fourth power machine and becomes sixteen
figure.caption: The fourth root reverses the same process.

blocks.hint: Write the repeated multiplication before evaluating.
blocks.solution:
The base is 2. The exponent 5 counts copies of the base.

Write \(2\times 2\times 2\times 2\times 2\). Multiply from left to right, one pair at a time.

\(2^{5}=32\).

retry.feedback: That multiplies the base by the exponent. The power calls for repeated copies of the base.

blocks.html: Swapping the base and exponent usually changes the result.

blocks.hint: Write the repeated multiplication before evaluating.
blocks.solution:
The base is 5. The exponent 6 counts copies of the base.

Write \(5\times 5\times 5\times 5\times 5\times 5\). Multiply from left to right, one pair at a time.

\(5^{6}=15625\).

retry.feedback: That multiplies the base by the exponent. The power calls for repeated copies of the base.

sections.title: What does the index on a root do?
sections.label: Reverse
sections.intro: Work backwards from the result. A fourth root asks for a base whose fourth power gives the number under the root sign. Similarly for other roots.

blocks.html: Check your root by raising it to the power shown by the small index.

blocks.hint: Decide which power you are reversing. Test a base by raising it to that power.
blocks.solution:
The small 5 tells you to reverse the 5th power.

Check \((-2)^{5}=-32\).

The value of the named root is \(-2\).

blocks.html: An even root of a positive number is written as the positive root. An odd root can be negative.

blocks.hint: Decide which power you are reversing. Test a base by raising it to that power.
blocks.solution:
The small 5 tells you to reverse the 5th power.

Check \(5^{5}=3125\).

The value of the named root is \(5\).

sections.title: Does the equation ask for more than one number?
sections.label: Solutions
sections.intro: Compare the root symbol with an equation in an even power. Two opposite bases give the same positive even power.

blocks.html: When the question says solve, check both signs and give all solutions.

blocks.hint: Check both the positive and negative base for an even power.
blocks.solution:
\(10^{6}=1000000\) gives one solution.

6 is even. Replacing the base by its negative leaves the same positive power.

The full answer is \(\{-10,10\}\). The root sign alone would give just 10.

retry.feedback: That is one solution. Its negative raised to the same even power gives the same result.

blocks.html: One correct value is incomplete if there is a second real solution.

blocks.hint: Check both the positive and negative base for an even power.
blocks.solution:
\(4^{4}=256\) gives one solution.

4 is even. Replacing the base by its negative leaves the same positive power.

The full answer is \(\{-4,4\}\). The root sign alone would give just 4.

retry.feedback: That is one solution. Its negative raised to the same even power gives the same result.

examples.title: Evaluate a higher power
examples.question: Work out \(2^{4}\) without a calculator.
solution: The base is 2. The exponent 4 counts copies of the base.
Write \(2\times 2\times 2\times 2\). Multiply from left to right, one pair at a time.

solution: The base is 6. The exponent 5 counts copies of the base.

solution: The small 5 tells you to reverse the 5th power.
The value of the named root is \(-3\).

solution: The small 6 tells you to reverse the 6th power.

solution: \(4^{6}=4096\) gives one solution.
6 is even. Replacing the base by its negative leaves the same positive power.
The full answer is \(\{-4,4\}\). The root sign alone would give just 4.

igcse-0580-powers-mixed.description: Break a mixed calculation into smaller steps and check the grouping.

sections.title: Which pieces should I work out first?
sections.label: Multiply
sections.intro: Mark each complete power and each complete root before multiplying. Replace each piece by its value.

blocks.html: Work out the powers and roots, then finish the multiplication.

figure.alt: One path evaluates a power and another evaluates a root. Their results go to a multiplication step.
figure.caption: Finish the two calculations before joining their results.

blocks.hint: Treat each power or root as one number, then multiply.
blocks.solution:
Calculate each power or root first.

The square is 121. The cube root is 4 because \(4^3=64\).

Multiply to give \(121\times4=484\).

blocks.html: A power or root can change the size by much more than its index suggests.

blocks.hint: Treat each power or root as one number, then multiply.
blocks.solution:
Calculate each power or root first.

The square is 196. The cube root is 5 because \(5^3=125\).

Multiply to give \(196\times5=980\).

sections.title: Where does the root bar end?
sections.label: Bar
sections.intro: Read the whole expression before you calculate. A term to the right of the end of the bar belongs outside the root.

blocks.html: Treat a root's bar as grouping, like brackets around the quantity under it.

blocks.hint: Read where the root bar ends, then evaluate each term.
blocks.solution:
Work out what the root sign covers. It stops before the plus sign.

The term under the root gives 10. The other term gives 25.

Add to get \(10+25=35\).

blocks.html: Do not include the next plus term unless the bar includes it.

blocks.hint: Read where the root bar ends, then evaluate each term.
blocks.solution:
Work out what the root sign covers. It stops before the plus sign.

The term under the root gives 13. The other term gives 49.

Add to get \(13+49=62\).

sections.title: What if the base is a fraction?
sections.label: Fractions
sections.intro: Write the bracketed fraction twice for a square or three times for a cube. Then use ordinary fraction multiplication.

blocks.html: Raise both the numerator and the denominator to the stated power.

blocks.hint: The brackets make the numerator and denominator part of the same base.
blocks.solution:
The whole fraction is inside brackets. Use 2 copies.

Multiply the top numbers together, and the bottom numbers together.

The result is \(\frac{4}{9}\).

retry.feedback: Apply the power to both the numerator and denominator.

blocks.html: If only the top changes, repeat the denominator too.

blocks.hint: The brackets make the numerator and denominator part of the same base.
blocks.solution:
The whole fraction is inside brackets. Use 3 copies.

Multiply the top numbers together, and the bottom numbers together.

The result is \(\frac{343}{64}\).

retry.feedback: Apply the power to both the numerator and denominator.

examples.title: Combine a power and a root
examples.question: Work out \(5^2\times\sqrt[3]{8}\) without a calculator.
solution: Calculate each power or root first.
The square is 25. The cube root is 2 because \(2^3=8\).
Multiply to give \(25\times2=50\).

examples.title: Combine a power and a root

Multiply to give \(81\times3=243\).

examples.title: Check the reach of the root bar
examples.question: Work out \(\sqrt{16}+2^2\).
solution: Work out what the root sign covers. It stops before the plus sign.
The term under the root gives 4. The other term gives 4.
Add to get \(4+4=8\).

solution: Work out what the root sign covers. It stops before the plus sign.
The term under the root gives 8. The other term gives 16.

examples.question: Work out \(\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^{2}\) exactly.
solution: The whole fraction is inside brackets. Use 2 copies.
Multiply the top numbers together, and the bottom numbers together.
The result is \(\frac{16}{25}\).

solution: The whole fraction is inside brackets. Use 2 copies.
Multiply the top numbers together, and the bottom numbers together.
The result is \(\frac{1}{4}\).

extraPractice.solution:
The whole fraction is inside brackets. Use 3 copies.

Multiply the top numbers together, and the bottom numbers together.

The result is \(\frac{125}{64}\).

revision.body:
Which pieces should I work out first?

Work out the powers and roots, then finish the multiplication.

Where does the root bar end?

Treat a root's bar as grouping, like brackets around the quantity under it.

What if the base is a fraction?

Raise both the numerator and the denominator to the stated power.
